citeinfo.title: Data from Methane Emission Measurements and Isotope Geochemistry Samples from Orphan Oil and Gas Wells on the Kevin-Sunburst Dome in Montana, U.S.A., from April 2021 to October 2023

descript.abstract: This dataset contains methane emissions measurements, gas compositions, and methane carbon isotope geochemistry analysis results from orphan oil and gas wells in the Kevin-Sunburst Dome in Toole County, Montana. Emissions measurements were taken between 2021 and 2023, and gas samples were collected in July, 2023.
descript.purpose: These measurements and geochemistry samples were collected to better understand the source of methane leaking from orphan wells and to elucidate the causes of variation in their emission rates.

idinfo.native:
Data was processed using Microsoft Windows 11 and Microsoft Excel 365.
The data are stored in the following files: Emissions Rate Measurements: KD_OW_Emissions_Data.csv (5 KB) Geochemistry Results: KD_OW_Geochemistry_Data.csv (6 KB) Methane Carbon Isotope Results: KD_OW_Isotope_Data.csv (1 KB)

attracc.attraccr:
Emissions measurement accuracy was validated several ways: (1) Certified and calibrated gas flow meters were used to perform the emissions measurements (2) Gas compositions used to convert the flow rates were obtained from analysis provided by certified and traceable laboratories (3) The emissions data were reviewed and periods where the gas flow meters were producing unusual or nonsensical results were excluded from calculations.
Samples were analyzed via gas chromatography with flame ionization and thermal conductivity detectors (GC-FID/TCD) for C1 to C5 alkanes, CO2, and other (H2, He, air components) gases with an analytical precision in the range of 1.2 % to 4 % relative standard deviation and lower concentration reporting limits ranging from 4.9 % (methane) to 0.05 % (hexane). Thirteen samples contained sufficient material for analysis of δ13C of methane using GC-IRMS (Ellis and Dias, 2022). Replicate samples were taken at several sites for quality control purposes. Bulk compositions were corrected for air mixing in chambers and wellbores by using the oxygen concentration as the tracer for the air component and removing the relative abundances of other air sourced gases. The samples ranged from 10 % to 90 % air, with samples from wells with lower emissions rates and where it was not possible to setup a static chamber having lower abundances of reservoir gases.

dataqual.logic: Results were verified by comparing field replicates, internal laboratory replicates, and review of the tabulated results for errors.
dataqual.complete: Measurements of emission rates and gas composition were collected from leaking orphan wells in the Kevin-Sunburst Dome in Toole County, Montana, between 2021 and 2023. Samples were collected directly from well bores open to the atmosphere, or from chambers placed over the wells to accumulate the leaking gases. A substantial portion of the gas samples was air, and cylinders sometimes had to be charged with helium to get sufficient pressure for analysis. The uncorrected concentrations were sometimes very low and uncertainties relative to samples of produced gases maybe larger as a result of the air mixing and oxidation processes in the environment.

procstep.procdesc: Emissions Rate Measurements were provided to the USGS in PDF Form, containing average rates in either cubic meters per day or cubic feet per hour, a plot of time series flow rates, and associated laboratory gas composition analysis.
The emissions rates were manually reviewed and the minimum and maximum flow rates were recorded.
The flow rates (minimum, average, maximum) were converted to methane emissions rate using the concentration of methane in the gas leaking from the well.
In July 2023, the USGS collected gas samples from all wells and submitted to the USGS Petroleum Geochemistry Research Laboratory in Denver, CO for analysis.
Results from laboratory analysis were reviewed and formatted into a machine readable data table by replacing blanks with data quality indicators.

overview.eaover: These data tables contained time series emission rate measurements from orphan wells and gas composition data. Gas composition and isotope analysis were made using methods described in Ellis and Dias, 2022).
overview.eadetcit:
Ellis, G.S., and Dias, R.F., 2022, Development of hydrocarbon gas reference materials for stable isotopic composition (δ13C and δ2H): U.S. Geological Survey Scientific Investigations Report 2021–5136, 22 p., https://doi.org/10.3133/sir20215136.
Well information was obtained from the Montana Board of Oil & Gas Conservation Commission (2024). https://bogapps.dnrc.mt.gov/dataminer/Wells/Wells.aspx.
